p.src: At this, Jingui twisted her neck aside, curled her lip, snorted twice through her nostrils, and clapped her hands with a cold laugh. “Who has ever smelled fragrance in a water-caltrop flower? If water caltrops are fragrant, what place does that leave for flowers that are truly aromatic? What utter nonsense!” Xiangling replied, “It is not only water-caltrop flowers. Even lotus leaves and seedpods have a fresh fragrance. It is not the same as the perfume of flowers, but if you savor it closely on a still day or quiet night, at dawn or around midnight, you will find that fragrance lovelier than any flower’s. Even water caltrops, fox nuts, reed leaves, and reed roots, when touched by wind and dew, give off a clean scent that refreshes the mind and spirit.” Jingui said, “By your account, then, orchids and cassia flowers do not smell so fine after all?” Carried away by the conversation, Xiangling forgot the taboo and answered at once, “The fragrance of orchids and cassia flowers is itself beyond comparison with that of other flowers.” Before she had finished, Jingui’s maid Baochan pointed hurriedly at Xiangling’s face and cried, “Shame on you! Shame on you! How could you actually say Mistress’s name aloud!” Xiangling suddenly realized her mistake and, deeply embarrassed, hastened to smile apologetically. “It slipped out while I was talking. Please do not take offense, Mistress.” Jingui laughed. “What does it matter? You are far too cautious. Only, I have always thought that the character ‘Xiang,’ meaning ‘fragrance,’ is not quite suitable. I mean to replace it with another. I wonder whether you would accept that?” Xiangling quickly replied with a smile, “How can you speak so, Mistress? My whole body and being now belong to you. How could you ask whether I accept so small a thing as changing my name? I am not worthy of such consideration. Whichever character you think best is the one I shall use.” Jingui laughed. “That is all very well, but I fear Miss Baochai might take it to heart and say, ‘So the name I gave her is not as good as yours? You have been here only a few days, yet already you overturn my decisions.’” Xiangling smiled. “There is something you do not know, Mistress. When I was first bought, I was meant to serve the old lady, and that was why Miss Baochai gave me my name. Later, when I began serving Master Xue, I no longer had anything to do with her. Now that you are here, I have even less to do with her. Besides, Miss Baochai is exceptionally sensible. How could such a trifle anger her?” Jingui said, “If that is so, the character ‘Qiu,’ meaning ‘autumn,’ would be more fitting than ‘Xiang.’ Water caltrops and their flowers both flourish in autumn. Does that not give the name a better basis than ‘fragrance’?” Xiangling replied, “Then let it be as you say, Mistress.” From then on, the first character of her name was changed to Qiu, and Baochai took no notice of it.

p.src: Xue Pan was by nature one who, having gained Long, coveted Shu. Now that he had married Jingui, he noticed that her maid Baochan possessed a certain prettiness and a charmingly flirtatious manner, and he often called for tea or water merely to tease and entice her. Baochan understood his intentions well enough, but she was afraid of Jingui and dared not act rashly, so she waited to see what her mistress would do. Jingui soon perceived what he wanted and thought, “I have been looking for a chance to bring Xiangling to heel, but could find no opening. Since he has now taken a fancy to Baochan, I shall give Baochan over to him for the present. He will certainly grow distant from Xiangling, and while they are estranged, I can deal with her as I please. Baochan was mine to begin with, so she will remain easy enough to manage afterward.” Her plan settled, she waited for a chance to put it into action.

p.src: One evening, when Xue Pan was slightly tipsy, he again ordered Baochan to pour him some tea. As Xue Pan took the bowl, he deliberately squeezed her hand. Baochan made a show of dodging him and quickly snatched her hand away. Between their two false moves, the tea bowl fell to the floor with a crash, splashing tea all over him and across the floor. Embarrassed, Xue Pan pretended that Baochan had failed to hold it properly. Baochan retorted, “It was you, Sir, who failed to take it properly.” Jingui gave a cold laugh. “You have both played your parts quite well. Do not imagine everyone else is a fool.” Xue Pan lowered his head and smiled without speaking, while Baochan blushed and went out. When it was time to retire, Jingui deliberately drove Xue Pan away to sleep elsewhere. “That will keep your greedy eyes from starving over what they crave.” Xue Pan merely laughed. Jingui said, “If there is something you want, tell me openly. This furtive fumbling is useless.” Hearing this, Xue Pan used his drunkenness to cover his shame, knelt on the bedding, and seized Jingui’s hand with a laugh. “My dear sister, if you will give Baochan to me, I shall do anything you ask. If you wanted a human brain, I would get you one.” Jingui laughed. “What nonsense you talk. If you desire someone, say so plainly and take her into your room, so that others need not witness anything indecent. What could I possibly want from you?” Delighted by these words, Xue Pan thanked her endlessly and that night exerted himself to the utmost as a husband in order to please Jingui. The next day he did not go out, but stayed at home pestering and cajoling Baochan, growing ever bolder. In the afternoon, Jingui deliberately went out, leaving the two of them alone together. Xue Pan immediately began pulling and pawing at Baochan. Baochan understood most of what had been arranged and, half resisting and half consenting, was just about to yield to him. But Jingui had deliberately been waiting for this. Judging that they must now be too entangled to part, she summoned a young maid called Xiao She’er. This little maid had served Jingui in her parents’ home from childhood. Because both her parents had died when she was young and no one looked after her, everyone called her Xiao She’er, and she was employed solely for heavy, menial work. Jingui had summoned her alone on purpose and instructed her, “Go and tell Qiuling to fetch my handkerchief from my room, but do not say the message came from me.” Xiao She’er obeyed, went straight to find Xiangling, and said, “Miss Ling, Mistress left her handkerchief in her room. Would it not be kind of you to fetch it and take it to her?” Xiangling had lately suffered repeated humiliation at Jingui’s hands. Unable to understand the reason, she had been exhausting every effort to restore herself to Jingui’s favor. On hearing this, she hurried to the room to fetch the handkerchief. Quite unprepared, she burst in just as the two were yielding to one another. Her ears and face flamed scarlet with shame, and she hurriedly turned away and fled.

p.src: Xue Pan believed that, since the affair had been openly sanctioned, he had no one to fear except Jingui. He had not even closed the door; and though he felt a little ashamed when Xiangling suddenly came in, he did not take it too seriously. Baochan, however, was habitually boastful and proud. On being caught by Xiangling, she wished the earth would swallow her up. She hurriedly pushed Xue Pan away and fled, complaining bitterly as she went that he had assaulted and forced her. Xue Pan had only just coaxed her to the point of yielding when Xiangling spoiled everything. All his excitement turned into furious rage, which he vented on Xiangling. Without allowing her to explain, he rushed out, spat at her twice, and cursed, “You filthy whore! What are you doing here, blundering about like a wandering ghost?” Sensing trouble, Xiangling had already fled in a few quick strides. When Xue Pan went back to look for Baochan, she had vanished, so in his fury he did nothing but curse Xiangling. After supper that evening he was pleasantly drunk. While bathing, he found the water a little too hot and scalded his feet; claiming that Xiangling had deliberately tried to harm him, he chased her stark naked and kicked and struck her several times. Though Xiangling had never before endured such humiliation and suffering, matters had come to such a pass that there was nothing she could say. She could only grieve and lament alone before going away.

p.src: By then Jingui had secretly arranged matters with Baochan: that night Xue Pan and Baochan were to consummate their union in Xiangling’s room, while Xiangling was ordered to come and sleep with Jingui. At first Xiangling refused. Jingui accused her of finding the place dirty, then of seeking an easy life and fearing the work of attending her at night. She also abused her, saying, “That master of yours, who has never seen anything of the world, falls in love with every woman he sees. He has taken possession of my maid, yet will not send you to me. What can he possibly intend? I suppose he means to drive me to my death.” When Xue Pan heard this, he feared that the affair with Baochan might fall through, so he hurried over and cursed Xiangling: “You ungrateful wretch! If you do not go at once, I’ll beat you!” Helpless, Xiangling gathered up her bedding and went. Jingui ordered her to spread it on the floor and sleep there. Xiangling had no choice but to obey. No sooner had she lain down than Jingui called for tea; a little later she ordered her legs massaged. She did this seven or eight times during the night, never letting Xiangling lie peacefully for even a moment. Xue Pan, meanwhile, prized Baochan as though he had obtained a rare treasure and paid no attention to anything else. Jingui was so incensed that she secretly vowed, “Enjoy yourself for a few days. Once I begin dealing with you at my leisure, do not blame me for what happens!” Thus she endured her resentment while devising schemes against Xiangling.

p.src: About half a month later, Jingui suddenly began feigning illness again, claiming that her heart ached unbearably and that she could not move her limbs. Physicians were summoned, but their treatments had no effect, and everyone said that Xiangling had made her ill with anger. After two days of commotion, a paper figure suddenly tumbled out of Jingui’s pillow. Her birth date and eight characters were written upon it, and five needles had been driven into its heart and the joints of its four limbs. This threw everyone into confusion. Treating it as startling news, they first reported it to Aunt Xue. Aunt Xue was immediately flustered, and Xue Pan naturally became even more frantic, demanding that everyone be tortured and questioned at once. Jingui laughed. “Why falsely accuse everyone? Most likely it is one of Baochan’s spells.” “She has hardly had a spare moment in your room lately,” said Xue Pan. “Why accuse an innocent person?” Jingui sneered. “Who could it be but her? Surely you do not think I did it myself! Even if there were someone else, who would dare enter my room?” “Xiangling follows you every day now,” said Xue Pan. “She is bound to know. We shall find out if we question her under torture first.” Jingui sneered. “Whoever you torture, do you suppose she will confess? In my opinion, we should simply pretend to know nothing and all wash our hands of it. It does not matter if they kill me with their spells; you will be glad of the chance to marry someone better. To speak honestly, it merely comes down to the three of you finding one of me too much.” As she spoke, she burst into bitter tears. Her words enraged Xue Pan still further. Snatching up a door bar, he rushed straight to Xiangling and, without allowing her to explain, struck her savagely about the head and face, insisting that she had cast the spell. Xiangling cried out that she was innocent. Aunt Xue ran over and rebuked him: “You have not even learned the truth, yet you are already beating her. This girl has served you for years. When has she ever failed to attend you thoughtfully and wholeheartedly? How could she now bring herself to do such a heartless thing? Find out what is right and wrong before you resort to violence.” Hearing her mother-in-law speak this way, Jingui feared that Xue Pan might waver and relent. She therefore wailed even more loudly, crying, “For more than half a month you have kept my Baochan for yourself and forbidden her to enter my room, leaving only Qiuling to sleep beside me. When I propose questioning Baochan under torture, you rush to defend her. And now, out of spite, you go and beat Xiangling. Once you have done me to death, you need only choose some rich and beautiful woman to marry. Why go to the trouble of playing all these tricks?” These words made Xue Pan still more agitated. Aunt Xue heard how Jingui used every sentence to coerce her son and saw the utterly vicious, shameless way she behaved; she found her thoroughly detestable. Unfortunately, her son lacked all firmness and had long since grown accustomed to submitting meekly to Jingui’s control. Now he had also taken up with the maid; yet Jingui called it an abduction and claimed for herself the credit of being a gentle wife who yielded her husband to another.

p.src: In the end, no one knew who had worked this nightmarish sorcery. As the common saying goes, “Even an upright magistrate finds family disputes hard to judge”; this was truly a bedchamber dispute that even a husband’s parents could not settle. Unable to resolve it, she could only vent her anger by berating Xue Pan: “You worthless wretch! Even a rutting dog has more decency than you! Who would have thought that, without a word to anyone, you would lay hands on the maid who came with your wife? Now she can accuse you of seizing her maid—how can you show your face in public? And when no one even knows who devised the scheme, you ignore right and wrong and simply beat people indiscriminately. I knew you were the sort to cast aside the old for the new; all the care I once devoted to you was wasted. If she is so unsatisfactory, you still may not beat her. I shall summon a slave broker at once and sell her; then your mind will be at peace.” With that, she ordered Xiangling, “Pack your things and come with me,” while sending someone out with the command, “Fetch a slave broker quickly. Sell her for whatever few taels she will bring, pull out this thorn in the flesh and nail in the eye, and let us all live in peace.” Seeing that his mother was truly angry, Xue Pan had already bowed his head. Hearing this, Jingui cried through the window, “Sell whomever you please, madam, but there is no need to implicate one person while speaking of another. Do you take me for some jealous shrew who cannot tolerate another woman? Why call her ‘a thorn in the flesh and a nail in the eye’? Whose nail is she, and whose thorn? If I truly resented her in the least, I would never have let him take even my own maid into his room.” At this, Aunt Xue trembled with rage and choked out, “What family observes rules like these? The mother-in-law is speaking here, while the daughter-in-law quarrels back through the window. And you call yourself the daughter of an old and respectable family! What are you shouting and screaming all that nonsense for?” Stamping his feet in desperation, Xue Pan cried, “Enough, enough! What a laughingstock we shall be if anyone hears!” Jingui decided that, having begun, she might as well go through with it, and she made an even wilder scene, shouting, “I am not afraid of being laughed at! Your concubine plots against me and harms me, yet I am supposed to fear people’s laughter! If nothing else will do, then keep her and sell me instead. Everyone knows that the Xue family is rich, that you use money at every turn to crush people, and that you have powerful relatives with whom to intimidate others. Why not act quickly—what are you waiting for? If you find me unsatisfactory, who told you to be so blind and come begging at our house over and over again? Now that I have come, bringing gold and silver as well, and you have seized every passably presentable girl who came with me, it is time to drive me out!” She screamed and wept, rolling and writhing on the floor and striking herself. In his distress, Xue Pan could neither scold nor coax her, neither beat her nor plead with her. He merely paced in and out, sighing and groaning and lamenting his ill fortune.

If you find me unsatisfactory, who told you to be so blind and come begging at our house over and over again?
Now that I have come, bringing gold and silver as well, and you have seized every passably presentable girl who came with me, it is time to drive me out!”
She screamed and wept, rolling and writhing on the floor and striking herself.
In his distress, Xue Pan could neither scold nor coax her, neither beat her nor plead with her. He merely paced in and out, sighing and groaning and lamenting his ill fortune.

p.src: By then, Baochai had already persuaded Aunt Xue to go inside, but she still ordered someone to come and sell Xiangling. Baochai smiled. “Our family has always known how to buy servants, but we have never heard of selling them. Mother, anger must have muddled your wits. If word of this gets out, will people not laugh at us? If Brother and Sister-in-law find her unsatisfactory, leave her to serve me. I happen to be short of help myself.” Aunt Xue replied, “If we keep her, she will only cause more trouble. It would be cleaner to send her away.” Baochai smiled. “It will amount to the same thing if she follows me; in any case, I shall not let her go to the front quarters. Once all contact with his quarters is severed, it will be as though she had been sold.” Xiangling had already run to Aunt Xue, weeping bitterly and begging not to be sent away, saying that she was willing to follow Baochai. Aunt Xue therefore had no choice but to relent. From that time on, Xiangling did indeed follow Baochai and resolutely cut off every path leading to the front quarters. Even so, she could not help grieving beneath the moon and sighing alone by lamplight. She was delicate by nature, and although she had spent several years in Xue Pan’s chamber, an ailment of the blood had prevented her from ever conceiving. Now anger and sorrow compounded her condition, and the afflictions from within and without became unbearable, eventually developing into a wasting disorder of the blood. Day by day she grew thinner and feverish, lost all appetite, and failed to improve despite examinations by physicians and courses of medicine. During this time, Jingui made several more scenes, reducing Aunt Xue and her daughter to secret tears and bitter complaints against fate. Xue Pan did confront her two or three times under the influence of drink. When he raised a cudgel to beat her, Jingui thrust her body toward him and told him to strike as he pleased; when he brandished a knife and threatened to kill her, she stretched out her neck to him. Xue Pan truly could not bring himself to do it, so after a bout of uproar the matter simply ended. As familiarity turned this into routine, Jingui grew ever more overbearing, while Xue Pan became ever more spineless. Although Xiangling was still there, it was as though she were not. Jingui could not feel entirely gratified, but Xiangling no longer offended her eye, so for the time being she let the matter rest. She then gradually began finding fault with Baochan. Baochan, however, was of a very different temperament from Xiangling. She was dry tinder to Xue Pan’s flame, and once the two had fallen in love, they put Jingui entirely out of mind. When she lately saw Jingui abusing her again, she refused to humble herself or yield by so much as an inch. At first they traded sharp words whenever they crossed paths; later, as Jingui’s fury mounted, she began to curse Baochan and finally to strike her. Though Baochan dared not answer back or retaliate, she would throw the wildest tantrums, tossing back her head and rolling on the floor while threatening suicide—brandishing knives and scissors by day and ropes by night, and stopping at nothing to create an uproar. Unable to attend to both women at once, Xue Pan could only hover uncertainly between them. When their uproar became utterly unmanageable, he would leave the house and hide in the outer quarters. When Jingui was not losing her temper and happened to be in good spirits, she would gather people together to play cards and throw dice for amusement.

p.src: All her life she had been especially fond of gnawing bones. Every day she insisted that chickens or ducks be slaughtered, gave the meat to others, and kept only the crisp-fried bones to accompany her wine. Whenever she tired of eating or became angry, she would let loose a torrent of abuse: “If other damned whores can enjoy themselves, why should I not!” Aunt Xue and Baochai paid her no attention at all. Xue Pan had no remedy either. Day and night he could only regret marrying this bane of the household, blaming it all on his momentary lack of judgment. Thus everyone in the Ning and Rong mansions, from the highest to the lowest, came to know of it, and not one failed to sigh over the affair.

p.src: By this time, Baoyu's hundred days of mourning were over, and he was going out again. He had also come to see Jingui and thought, “There is nothing fierce or forbidding in her bearing or appearance. She is as fresh and lovely as any flower or tender willow, and no less attractive than any of the other girls. How, then, could she possess such a temperament? It is strange in the extreme.” This left him greatly perplexed. One day, when he went to pay his respects to Lady Wang, he happened to meet Yingchun's old nurse, who had returned to the house to pay her respects. She spoke of Sun Shaozu's thoroughly disgraceful conduct and said, “All the young mistress can do is weep and wipe away her tears in secret. She only wishes to be brought home so that she may relax for a couple of days.” Lady Wang said, “I have been meaning to bring her home during these next few days, but one thing after another has gone awry, and so it slipped my mind. Baoyu went there the other day and told me about it when he returned. Tomorrow is an auspicious day, so we shall bring her home then.” While they were still speaking, Grandmother Jia sent someone to fetch Baoyu, saying, “Tomorrow morning, first thing, you are to go to the Temple of the Great Emperor of the Eastern Peak to redeem our vow.” Baoyu now longed for any chance to go out and amuse himself. On hearing this, he was so delighted that he did not close his eyes all night, impatient for dawn to come.

p.src: Early the next morning, after washing, dressing, and making himself ready, he set out by carriage with two or three elderly matrons, passing through the west city gate to burn incense and redeem the vow at the Temple of the Great Emperor of the Eastern Peak. Everything at the temple had been made ready the day before. Baoyu was timid by nature and dared not approach the ferocious images of gods and demons. This temple had been built during the preceding dynasty and was exceedingly grand. But after so many years, it had also become exceedingly desolate. The clay images within were all extremely fearsome, so he hurriedly burned the paper horses and spirit money, then withdrew to the Taoist quarters to rest. After they had eaten, the matrons, Li Gui, and the others gathered around Baoyu and accompanied him as he wandered about and amused himself for a while. When Baoyu grew tired, he returned to a quiet room to rest. Afraid that he might fall asleep, the matrons asked the old Taoist Wang, who managed the temple, to come and keep him talking. This old Taoist Wang made a particular business of selling medicines, peddling secret prescriptions picked up in his travels to cure people and make a profit. A signboard hung outside the temple, advertising pills, powders, plasters, and elixirs of every kind. He was also a familiar visitor at both the Ning and Rong mansions, where everyone had given him the nickname “Wang One-Plaster,” meaning that his plasters were so efficacious that a single application would cure every ailment. Presently Wang One-Plaster came in. Baoyu was reclining on the kang and about to fall asleep, while Li Gui and the others were teasing and cajoling him, saying, “Young master, don't go to sleep.” When they saw Wang One-Plaster enter, they all laughed and cried, “You've come at just the right time! Just the right time! Master Wang, you are so good at telling old tales. Tell one for our young master to hear.” Wang One-Plaster laughed. “Quite right. Don't sleep, young master, or mind the sinews in your belly don't start making mischief.” At this, everyone in the room burst out laughing. Baoyu also laughed, sat up, and straightened his clothes. Wang One-Plaster loudly ordered his apprentices to brew some good strong tea at once. Mingyan said, “Our young master won't drink your tea. Even sitting in this room, he complains about the smell of plasters.” Wang One-Plaster laughed. “What nonsense! The plasters are never brought into this room. Knowing that the young master was certain to come today, we began fumigating it with incense three or five days ago and have done so again and again.” Baoyu said, “Indeed. I hear every day how wonderful your plasters are, but what illnesses do they actually cure?” Wang One-Plaster replied, “If you ask about my plasters, young master, that is a long story. Their subtle principles cannot be exhausted in a few words. They contain altogether one hundred and twenty ingredients: sovereign and minister support one another, host and guest are properly matched, warming and cooling drugs are used together, and costly and common ingredients each have their distinct prescriptions. Internally, they restore the vital constitution and replenish the qi, stimulate the appetite, nourish the nutritive and defensive energies, calm the spirit and settle the mind, dispel cold and heat, aid digestion, and dissolve phlegm. Externally, they harmonize the blood vessels, relax the sinews and channels, remove dead flesh and generate new tissue, expel wind, and disperse toxins. Their efficacy is miraculous; anyone who has used one knows it.” Baoyu said, “I don't believe that a single plaster can cure all those illnesses. Let me ask you, then: there is one particular illness—can your plaster cure that too?”

p.src: Wang Yitie said, “There is no illness or affliction on which it does not work at once. If it fails, young master, you may seize me by the beard, slap this old face of mine, and tear down my temple—how would that be? You need only tell me the cause of the ailment.” Baoyu laughed. “You guess. If you guess correctly, your plaster will have cured it.” Hearing this, Wang Yitie pondered for a while, then laughed. “That is hard to guess. I fear my plaster may not be quite so effective after all.” Baoyu told Li Gui and the others, “Go outside and amuse yourselves for a while. With so many people in this room, it is growing more stifling and foul by the moment.” At this, Li Gui and the others went out to do as they pleased, leaving only Mingyan behind. Mingyan held a lighted stick of Sweet-Dream incense. Baoyu had him sit at his side and leaned against him. Something stirred in Wang Yitie's mind. He came closer with a grin and whispered, “I believe I have guessed it. I suppose that now the young master has begun having affairs in his chamber, you want a strengthening medicine. Am I right?” Before he had finished, Mingyan shouted, “Damn you! Slap your mouth!” Baoyu still did not understand and hurriedly asked, “What did he say?” “Pay no attention to his nonsense,” said Mingyan. Frightened, Wang Yitie dared ask no more and merely said, “Then please tell me plainly, young master.” Baoyu said, “Tell me, have you any prescription that can cure a woman's jealousy?” At this, Wang Yitie clapped his hands and laughed. “Now you have defeated me. Not only do I have no prescription for it, I have never even heard of one.” Baoyu laughed. “Then you are not much of a physician after all.” Wang Yitie hastily continued, “I have never encountered a plaster for jealousy, but there is a medicinal broth that might cure it. It works slowly, though, and cannot produce an immediate result.” Baoyu asked, “What broth is that, and how is it taken?” Wang Yitie said, “It is called Jealousy-Curing Broth. Take one fine autumn pear, two qian of rock sugar, one qian of dried tangerine peel, and three bowls of water; simmer them until the pear is cooked. Eat one such pear every morning, and if you keep eating them, you will eventually recover.” Baoyu said, “That costs next to nothing, but I doubt it will work.” Wang Yitie said, “If one dose does not work, take ten. If it does not work today, take it again tomorrow; if it does not work this year, keep taking it until next year. In any case, these three ingredients moisten the lungs, stimulate the appetite, and do no harm. They are sweet, suppress coughs, and taste delicious besides. Once she has eaten it past the age of a hundred, she will have to die sooner or later—and when she is dead, how can she still be jealous? That is when the medicine will have taken effect.” At this, Baoyu and Mingyan laughed without cease and called him a “glib-tongued ox-head.” Wang Yitie laughed. “I was merely helping you while away your noonday drowsiness. What harm is there in that? If my jokes make you laugh, they have served their purpose. To tell you the truth, even my plasters are fake.

p.src: By then Yingchun had been home for quite some time. The matrons and married servants of the Sun household had been served supper and sent back. Yingchun was tearfully pouring out her grievances in Lady Wang's room. She said that Sun Shaozu “is consumed by lust, addicted to gambling and drink, and has violated nearly every married servant and maid in the household. When I tried to remonstrate with him two or three times, he cursed me as ‘a woman wrung out of a jar of vinegar.’ He also said that Father had once taken five thousand taels of silver from him and had no right to spend it. Now he has demanded it back two or three times without success, so he pointed in my face and said, ‘Do not put on the airs of a fine lady with me. Your father spent five thousand taels of my silver, so you were handed over to me in payment, as good as bought. Whenever I please, I can have you beaten and driven off to sleep in the servants' quarters. When your grandfather was alive, he coveted our wealth and influence and eagerly sought our acquaintance. Properly speaking, your father and I are of the same generation, yet now he has forced me beneath him and made me his junior for life. I should never have made this marriage either; it only makes people think I am some snob chasing power and position.’” She sobbed as she spoke, and Lady Wang and all the young ladies shed tears with her. Lady Wang could only offer words of comfort. “Since you have encountered such an unreasonable man, what can be done? At the time, your uncle tried to dissuade your father from arranging this marriage. But your father stubbornly refused to listen and insisted on having his way; in the end, it has indeed turned out badly. My child, this too is your fate.” Yingchun wept. “I cannot believe my fate is truly so wretched! I lost my mother when I was little, but fortunately I spent several peaceful years here with you, Aunt. And now I have come to such an end!” As Lady Wang consoled her, she asked where she would like to stay. Yingchun replied, “Having so recently parted from my sisters, I think of them sleeping and waking. Besides, I still miss my own rooms. If I could stay three or five days in my old quarters in the Garden, I would be content even to die. Who knows whether I shall ever be able to stay there again?” Lady Wang hurriedly urged her, “Do not speak such nonsense. Young married couples bickering and trading sharp words is commonplace in countless households. Why utter such ominous things?” She promptly ordered the rooms at Purple Caltrop Isle to be prepared, told the young ladies to keep Yingchun company and console her, and instructed Baoyu, “You must not let the slightest word of this reach the Old Lady. If she learns of any of it, I shall know that you told her.” Baoyu repeatedly assented and obeyed. That night Yingchun once more slept in her old residence. All the young ladies treated her with exceptional affection. She stayed for three days in succession before going to Lady Xing's quarters. First she took leave of Grandmother Jia and Lady Wang, then parted from all her sisters; everyone was deeply grieved and reluctant to let her go.

First she took leave of Grandmother Jia and Lady Wang, then parted from all her sisters; everyone was deeply grieved and reluctant to let her go.

p.src: Only after Lady Wang, Aunt Xue, and the others comforted and persuaded them did their tears subside, and Yingchun went over to Lady Xing's quarters. After she had stayed two days with Lady Xing, servants sent by Sun Shaozu came to fetch her. Though Yingchun did not wish to go, she feared Sun Shaozu's cruelty and had no choice but to suppress her feelings, force herself to bid farewell, and depart. Lady Xing had never much cared. She neither asked whether the couple lived in harmony nor concerned herself with Yingchun's domestic troubles, but merely went through the motions for appearance's sake. How matters ultimately turned out is not yet known; listen to the explanation in the next chapter.
